findings.evidence: Refuter: build_analysis.py:252-261 (after = x.loc[low_day:]); make_charts.py:195-196 ('after its lowest point in the episode'); gate.toml:81. Computed, checks_r2_logic_out.txt section A: Bitcoin closed at or above 9,636.00 on 2020-02-21 (2 days); 47,223.65 against 46,453.43 on 2022-03-28 (58 days); 98,392.22 against 96,647.91 on 2025-02-20 (1 day). The S&P figures 126, 513, 89 are right because the S&P cannot regain before its own trough. Adjudicator: build_analysis.py:255-261: regain_days sets low_day = window.idxmin() over high to S&P low and searches after = x.loc[low_day:], so it counts to the first close at or above the high-day level AFTER the asset's low, not the first close back. My runs (adj-logic/check_b1_out.txt, check_b1b_out.txt, on build_analysis.daily_prices): 2020, Bitcoin closed below its 19 Feb level (9,636.00) on 20 Feb and back on 21 Feb, 2 trading days (post says 55); 2022, below its 3 Jan level (46,453.43) on 4 Jan and back on 2022-03-28 at 47,223.65, 58 trading days (post says 505); 2025, first close below on 21 Feb and first close back on 2025-05-02, 51 days, which matches only because Bitcoin did not close back before its 8 April low. So two of the three Bitcoin figures are false as written, not all three: the refuter's 1 day for 2025 counts a close that never left the level, which is not 'closed back'. S&P 126, 513, 89 hold under both readings. The next sentence, 'In the 2022 episode they were close', is also false under the stated measure (58 against 513). The sentence contradicts the sh-3 footnote (make_charts.py:195-196, PNG viewed). Round 1 stats:F2's adjudicator premise ('counts the first close') is wrong per line 259; the r1 wording 'got back to its starting level' was looser and not false in this way.
